rows.description: A toddler bangs a spoon, claps or refuses a food because the child beside them does. This is pure imitation with no idea of rules or approval, yet it is the root of later fitting in.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A child insists on the same bottle colour, the same game rules and the same dance step as the group. Sameness feels safe and being different feels like being left out.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A child stops admitting they like a certain cartoon or song once classmates mock it. They feel a small betrayal of themselves but relief at not standing out.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.subtype: Changing an answer after others answer [Actor]
rows.description: A child who knew the right answer changes it when most of the class says otherwise. Doubting oneself feels easier than being the lone voice, even when privately certain.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A child with a homemade tiffin, a regional accent or older clothes is laughed at. They may shrink, copy the group or quietly resent it, learning early that difference carries a price.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A teenager takes up the group's slang, brands and risky dares to belong. Publicly compliant and privately doubtful, they mistake being accepted for being known.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A teenager is told that skipping class, vaping or a prank is what everyone does, with a hint of exclusion if they refuse. The threat is social, so it feels bigger than the act itself.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 18–22, 23–26

rows.subtype: Sudden shifts in taste and friends [Observer]
rows.description: A parent notices new slang, music and a new friend circle. Curiosity and steady interest work better than ridicule, which pushes the teen further into the group.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A teenager says a relaxed no thanks, not for me, without a lecture, and finds one friend who feels the same. Even one ally makes dissent far easier to sustain.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A new college student drifts into the hostel's habits of late nights, drinking or abstaining, and shared opinions. Away from family, the peer group becomes the main mirror for who they are.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 23–26
